title: Rowland Suisa (R. Suisa): The Prophet of Naga Peace, Democracy, and Customary Rights
alternate_titles: R. Suisa: The Life and Vision of a Tangkhul Thinker
Suisa's Proposal: Peace, Autonomy, and Peaceful Coexistence
subject: Biography (Jeevani), Political Philosophy & Peacebuilding
notes: Intellectual and political biography of Rowland Suisa (1907-1971), MP from Outer Manipur (1957-1962), author of the famous 'Suisa's Proposal' advocating peaceful negotiated settlement and honorable co-existence.

front_matter.title_page: Rowland Suisa (R. Suisa): The Prophet of Naga Peace, Democracy, and Customary Rights (2008)
front_matter.preface: Rowland Suisa was one of the most original political thinkers of Northeast India. Born in Somdal village, he served as Member of Parliament and dedicated his life to bridging differences between the Government of India and Naga national aspirations through constitutional federation and peaceful coexistence.

chapters.title: Early Life in Somdal & Educational Leadership
chapters.summary: Youth in Somdal, education in Jorhat and Shillong, and pioneer community organizing.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 1: Rowland Suisa 1907-li Somdal village, Ukhrul district-li pharisaye. Ana Jorhat Christian high school kala Shillongli education khuiye. Somdal-li unglaga ana Tangkhul youth, teachers, kala farmersbingli organize saye. Ana tribal customary law kala modern constitutional democracy-wui ngachaili philosophical harmony theitserie.
chapters.english_translation: Rowland Suisa was born in 1907 in Somdal village, Ukhrul district. He studied at Jorhat Christian High School and in Shillong. Returning to Somdal, he organized teachers, youths, and farmers, discovering a deep philosophical harmony between tribal customary law and modern constitutional democracy.

chapters.title: Parliamentary Career & The Famous 'Suisa's Proposal'
chapters.summary: Election to the 2nd Lok Sabha (1957) and the formulating of Suisa's historic peace proposal.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 2: 1957-li R. Suisa Outer Manipur constituency eina 2nd Lok Sabha-li MP elect saye. Parliament-li ana hill tribeswui rights, autonomy, kala economic justice-wui vang speak saye. Ana historical 'Suisa's Proposal' formulate saye: India kala Nagaswui ngachaili federal association eina honorable peaceful co-existence kasakakhui. Nehru kala Jayaprakash Narayan-na awui vision-li high respect miye.
chapters.english_translation: In 1957, R. Suisa was elected Member of Parliament to the 2nd Lok Sabha. In Parliament, he passionately voiced the rights, autonomy, and aspirations of hill tribal peoples. He drafted the historic 'Suisa's Proposal', outlining an honorable federal association ensuring peaceful co-existence. National leaders including Prime Minister Nehru and Jayaprakash Narayan deeply respected his visionary statesmanship.
exercises: What was the core concept of Suisa's Proposal?

chapters.title: Legacy of Peaceful Dialogue and Democratic Philosophy
chapters.summary: Final years, passing in 1971, and enduring moral inspiration for peace in the Naga hills.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 3: R. Suisana April 17, 1971 zingsho eina shok-unglakna. Awui life and writingsna chitheiye: True peace violence eina rara mashuk-mana; it must be built upon mutual respect, justice, and democratic federation. Awui thoughts modern Naga peace process-li guiding light thada leisaye.
chapters.english_translation: R. Suisa passed away on April 17, 1971. His life and philosophical writings proved that true peace cannot be achieved through violence, but must be constructed on mutual respect, justice, and democratic federation. His ideas continue to serve as a beacon for the ongoing peace process in the region.
exercises: Explain R. Suisa's enduring relevance for peace studies in Northeast India.

In 1957, R. Suisa was elected Member of Parliament to the 2nd Lok Sabha.
In Parliament, he passionately voiced the rights, autonomy, and
aspirations of hill tribal peoples. He drafted the historic 'Suisa's
Proposal', outlining an honorable federal association ensuring peaceful
co-existence. National leaders including Prime Minister Nehru and
Jayaprakash Narayan deeply respected his visionary statesmanship.
